tool_args.rationale: The pilot is already at the target horizon of 0.6, but it never enters the proposed activation regime. The 2.0-cost open-branch probe is the least expensive listed measurement aimed at distinguishing continued smooth behavior from an activated sink.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the recalled threshold siphon model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five sink gradients are at or below 2.20, below the recalled onset range of 2.50–2.68. The pilot cannot constrain either the onset or the strength of the activated sink.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a stationary Cobb–Douglas or Haldane law
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Cobb–Douglas imposes a smooth gradient effect with no onset, while Haldane ignores the gradient. The pilot varies input and gradient together, so it cannot reliably distinguish those explanations from a gated sink.
It costs more and targets trajectory resolution rather than the immediate ambiguity about sink activation.
